title: Reduced motion and accessible animation
learningObjectives: Explain reduced motion and accessible animation and apply the concept in maintainable CSS.

understand.concept: Accessible animation keeps essential information available without motion and respects user preferences such as prefers-reduced-motion. Avoid flashing, rapid movement, and interactions that require motion to understand. Provide a clear static state when animation is disabled.
understand.whyItMatters: Some users experience discomfort or other effects from motion. A reduced-motion rule should remove or simplify non-essential animation without removing content or feedback.
understand.analogy: An accessible animation offers a still version of the same message, so the user can choose a comfortable presentation.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; actual cascade, inheritance, and rendering follow CSS specifications.

explain.narrative: The decorative pulse stops for reduced-motion users while the message remains visible.

examples.explanation: The decorative pulse stops for reduced-motion users while the message remains visible.

practise.guidedTask: Add reduced-motion handling to a decorative animation. Ensure the state is also communicated with text or an icon that does not depend on movement.
practise.independentTask: Build a small component or page section that uses the concept. Test alternate content and, where relevant, right-to-left direction or reduced-motion settings.
hints: Inspect computed styles and inherited values.
Change one declaration at a time.
Keep user preferences and writing direction in mind.

questions.prompt: What must remain available when non-essential motion is disabled?
options: The content and meaning of the interface
questions.answer: The content and meaning of the interface
questions.explanation: Reduced motion should not remove the information or interaction the animation was decorating.

questions.prompt: What is a maintainable way to use CSS features across a project?
options: Use clear reusable rules and test computed behaviour
Copy unrelated declarations into every component
Ignore writing direction and user preferences
questions.answer: Use clear reusable rules and test computed behaviour
questions.explanation: Reusable CSS should remain understandable and work across relevant content and user settings.
